title: Pipe-highlight radius compares tile-unit distances against a pixel-unit radius — every pipe on the map pulses
evidence:
+SPAWN_HIGHLIGHT_RADIUS_TILES :: 8 // pipes within this of the new node pulse
+		rad := f32(SPAWN_HIGHLIGHT_RADIUS_TILES) * v.tile_px
+			ma := topo.node_pos[sa]
+			mb := topo.node_pos[sb]
+			mid := [2]i32{(ma[0] + mb[0]) / 2, (ma[1] + mb[1]) / 2}
+			dx := f32(mid[0]) - f32(r.pos[0])
+			dy := f32(mid[1]) - f32(r.pos[1])
+			if dx * dx + dy * dy > rad * rad {
detail: dx/dy are tile-coordinate deltas (node_pos values); rad is 8×tile_px in pixels. Comparing tiles² against px² inflates the effective radius to 8×tile_px tiles — on the 40×30 map every alive pipe passes, not pipes within 8 tiles.
recommended_fix: Compare in one space: drop '* v.tile_px' and test against 8.0 in tile units, or convert both endpoints via node_screen before the distance test.

title: Reduced-motion disables the pipe highlight entirely, contradicting the promised 'steady band'
detail: The proc's own doc, the file header ('the highlight is steady'), and the PR body ('the highlight steady — presence, not motion') all promise a pinned static band; the early return removes the placement feedback entirely under reduced motion.
recommended_fix: When reduced_motion is set, draw the band at a fixed steady alpha (the k=0 reading) instead of returning.

title: Type-chip hairline now fades via line alpha, which the diff itself says the software renderer ignores
evidence:
// the paper chip + ink hairline (full-alpha — the rlsw line-alpha trap)
-	out.a = 255
+	out.a = u8(255 * fade)
-	rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx({x0, y0}, {cw, ch}, max(1.0, s * 0.02), out)
+	rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx({x0, y0}, {cw, ch}, max(1.0, s * 0.02 * reveal_scale), out)
+| Ring/highlight as filled geometry (pinned table + quads), not lines | The rlsw software renderer ignores line alpha — a fading line would capture solid. |
detail: During the reveal the chip outline fades via DrawRectangleLinesEx alpha, but rlsw ignores line alpha — golden captures render it solid while the GPU app fades it. The adjacent comment still claims full-alpha.
recommended_fix: Keep the hairline full-alpha per the documented trap, or redraw it as filled quads so the fade survives the software renderer; update the stale comment.

title: spawn_fx_init and spawn_fx_destroy have no call sites in the diff
detail: Spawn_FX is a brand-new View field, so no pre-existing code can call these; the diff adds none. The reveals buffer therefore allocates via the ambient context on first append and is never destroyed.
recommended_fix: Wire spawn_fx_init/spawn_fx_destroy into View setup/teardown (app + harness), or delete the unused procs.

title: Dedup-reset branch in spawn_fx_predict can never fire
detail: predicted_window is only assigned after passing the lead≤10 gate for that same window value; with monotonic ticks and a fixed interval, predicted_window == window cannot hold when lead > 10 — the 'reset' is dead and its comment misleading.
recommended_fix: Delete the branch — the dedup already self-resets because the stored window differs from the next window.

title: Pointless '_ = before' no-op in the feed test
evidence:
+	before := len(s.events) - 1 // the last event is the t80 NODE_SPAWNED
+	_ = before
+	slice := s.events[before:]
detail: '_ = before' is a dead assignment immediately before 'before' is actually used — leftover scaffolding that obscures the slice-discipline intent.
recommended_fix: Drop the '_ = before' line; optionally assert the slice's last event tag is EVENT_TAG_NODE_SPAWNED to pin the assumption.

title: Telegraph timeline guard underflows when spawn_tick < SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS
detail: T is u64; T-10 wraps when the growth window is below tick 10 (interval is only checked > 0 in spawn_fx_predict), making 'tick < wrapped' always true — the telegraph silently never draws for early windows.
recommended_fix: Compute the bound in i64 (i64(T) - SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS), or clamp terminal_spawn_interval_ticks >= SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS at catalog load.

title: PR claims 'no transcendentals in the raster path' but the new highlight calls rl.Vector2Length
evidence:
+			l := rl.Vector2Length(d)
+determinism rule: no transcendentals in the raster path (the ring is a pinned
detail: Vector2Length is a sqrt in the new raster path; the in-code comment leans on an existing precedent ('already in the raster path'), leaving the PR's blanket §10.4 claim inaccurate for this code.
recommended_fix: Qualify the PR claim (pinned table for the ring only) or replace Vector2Length with an approved deterministic path if §10.4 is strict.

title: Reveal envelope never reaches k=1 — visible settle pop at expiry
detail: Last visible age is 7/8: smoothstep(0.875)≈0.957 → scale 0.974, fade 0.970, then the normal draw snaps to 1.0 — a ~2.6% pop at settle. The ring burst does reach k=1; the reveal does not.
recommended_fix: Include age == SPAWN_REVEAL_TICKS in the window (k=1 → exactly 1.0/1.0) so the envelope lands before expiry.
